reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / Bradley's Neurology in Clinical Practice
clinicalPearls: A late (tertiary) form of neurosyphilis caused by Treponema pallidum, developing years to decades after untreated infection
Results from degeneration of the dorsal columns and dorsal roots, producing a progressive sensory ataxia with a broad-based, stamping gait
Lightning pains, lancinating paroxysms in the limbs or trunk, are a characteristic feature
Loss of proprioception and vibration causes a positive Romberg sign, and deep tendon reflexes are often absent
The Argyll Robertson pupil accommodates but does not react to light and is a classic associated sign
Impaired pain and position sense can lead to painless Charcot joints and trophic foot ulcers
Visceral crises, such as sudden severe abdominal pain, and bladder dysfunction may occur
Diagnosis rests on positive serum and cerebrospinal fluid treponemal testing, and penicillin-based therapy halts progression but may not reverse established deficits
reference.pathophysiology: Chronic infection with Treponema pallidum leads, in the tertiary phase, to inflammatory degeneration of the posterior (dorsal) columns and the dorsal nerve roots and ganglia. Loss of large sensory fibres carrying proprioception and vibration produces sensory ataxia, areflexia, and the characteristic gait, while dorsal root involvement generates the lancinating lightning pains. The associated pupillary and autonomic findings reflect more widespread involvement of the nervous system. The condition is now rare where syphilis is treated early but persists in undertreated populations and those with HIV co-infection.
additionalDifferentials: Subacute combined degeneration from vitamin B12 deficiency
Other causes of dorsal column dysfunction and sensory ataxia
additionalInvestigations: Serum treponemal and non-treponemal serology (e.g. TPPA and RPR/VDRL)
Cerebrospinal fluid examination including CSF-VDRL, cell count, and protein
HIV testing given frequent co-infection and altered natural history
MRI of the spine to demonstrate posterior column change and exclude other myelopathy
Nerve conduction studies to characterise the sensory involvement
redFlags: New or evolving neurological deficits in a patient with untreated or inadequately treated syphilis
Concurrent HIV infection, which accelerates and complicates neurosyphilis
Visceral crises or autonomic dysfunction requiring exclusion of other acute pathology
Neuropathic joint destruction or non-healing trophic ulcers indicating advanced sensory loss
reference.prognosis: Antibiotic treatment arrests further progression and treats active infection, but long-established dorsal column and root damage often persists, so residual ataxia, pain, and pupillary abnormalities are common; earlier treatment yields better outcomes.
pitfalls: Overlooking syphilis as a cause of sensory ataxia in the modern era
Confusing the picture with B12 deficiency and not sending treponemal serology
Failing to test for and address concurrent HIV infection
Misattributing lightning pains to a primary painful neuropathy
Expecting antibiotics to reverse fixed neurological deficits and neglecting supportive care
management: Parenteral penicillin using a neurosyphilis regimen, namely intravenous aqueous crystalline penicillin, as the specific antitreponemal treatment
Penicillin desensitisation in allergic patients, as penicillin remains the only reliable agent for neurosyphilis
Neuropathic and lightning-pain control with anticonvulsant agents such as carbamazepine
Physiotherapy and gait rehabilitation with walking aids for sensory ataxia
Protective foot care and orthopaedic management of trophic ulcers and Charcot joints from loss of protective sensation
Follow-up cerebrospinal fluid examination and serial serology to confirm treatment response
HIV testing and co-management given frequent co-infection and altered natural history, with ophthalmology input for pupillary abnormalities
